answer: Epoch-Summit Consistency Ledger: each epoch, agents submit an action summary backed by a cumulative history hash. Admission to the next epoch requires the new summary to match the prior hash at a juniper threshold of divergent records. Any identity failing the check is quarantined and its history frozen as a relic. Attackers must therefore sustain coherent per-identity histories across every epoch, paying continuous compute and storage per fake identity rather than a one-time cost.
